evals.name: tokens-from-direction-shadcn
evals.prompt: Can you turn DESIGN.md into proper design tokens and hook the app up to them? Light and dark both need to work.
evals.expected_output: A single token source with designed light and dark values, and the shadcn/ui variables in src/index.css (or a file it imports) set from it, so the existing Button, Card, muted text, the column-header strip and the DayLoad bar take the new theme. The values stay in the form every consumer reads: tailwind.config.js wraps each variable in hsl(var(--x)), and so do the inline styles in src/features/appointments/DayLoad.tsx, so oklch or hex in those variables breaks colours; ADR-0001's Safari 15.0 floor rules out oklch without an sRGB fallback. The run notices the header toggle sets data-theme="dark" while the dark variables sit under .dark and Tailwind uses darkMode class, so dark mode never worked, makes them agree, and deals with the theme being applied in an effect after first paint (dark users see a light flash on every load). It measures the direction's brand green #2BB673 with a white label at about 2.6:1, and as link text and focus ring on white, keeps the green hue but ships passing pairs, including the hover fills of the default and destructive Buttons (bg-primary/90 and bg-destructive/90 composited on the card) and muted text on the bg-muted header strip, and tells the user as a proposal for the owner of DESIGN.md (the operations lead, per README.md), which stays byte for byte as agreed; the proposal also names any dark-theme label that is not white. The DayLoad bar keeps at least 3:1 against its track. A check run by make check recomputes the contrast pairs, hover fills included, or the missing guard is named. Neutrals become warm (including the slate theme-color in index.html), cards lose their shadow, Inter stays the face the direction names, the 15 px body and tabular times are applied or named. It raises that the 36 px sm buttons are under a touch target on the front-desk iPads. It does not silently change Tailwind's default scales, weights or the radius steps; any such change is reported by its effect on the whole app. make check still passes; the Vite build cannot run here (no node_modules, no network) and there is no Safari 15 device, so both are stated as not done, the second by naming the Safari 15.0 floor. Nothing committed.
expectations: The colour values the app uses are defined once (one tokens file, or src/index.css itself) with separate light and dark values, and the shadcn/ui variables the components read (--background, --foreground, --card, --primary, --primary-foreground, --muted, --muted-foreground, --destructive, --border, --ring and the others in src/index.css) are set from them; the slate defaults from `npx shadcn init` no longer supply the app's colours; and the dark theme is its own set of values, not the light values inverted or left identical (at least background, card, foreground and border differ between the two modes)

Every consumer of the colour variables still gets a valid colour: tailwind.config.js wraps them as hsl(var(--x)) and src/features/appointments/DayLoad.tsx writes hsl(var(--primary)) and hsl(var(--primary) / 0.15) in inline styles, so each variable either still holds space-separated hue, saturation and lightness, or every one of those consumers is changed consistently; a variable holding oklch(...), a hex value or a full hsl(...) call while any consumer still wraps it in hsl() does not pass

No colour the app needs depends on a feature Safari 15.0 lacks (ADR-0001), in particular oklch() (Safari 15.4) or color-mix(), unless an sRGB fallback that Safari 15.0 renders is declared first for the same property outside the custom property (a custom property holding a hex then an oklch value keeps the oklch value and does not fall back); oklch kept only in a documentation or token source file that the app does not load is fine

The run notices that src/components/theme-toggle.tsx sets data-theme="dark" on the html element while the dark variables are under .dark in src/index.css and tailwind.config.js uses darkMode ["class"], so the toggle never switched the colours, and says so in the final message

After the run the dark values apply when the toggle is set to dark: the selector carrying the dark variables matches what theme-toggle.tsx sets, and Tailwind's dark variant uses the same selector (for example darkMode ["selector", '[data-theme="dark"]'], or the toggle changed to add the dark class), with both files consistent

A user whose saved choice or system setting is dark does not get the light theme on first paint: the theme is applied before the app renders (for example an inline script in index.html that sets the attribute from localStorage and matchMedia before the bundle loads) or the CSS applies the dark values under prefers-color-scheme: dark when no choice is stored; or the final message names the light flash on load (the theme is set in a useEffect after the first render) as not done

The primary button pair (--primary behind --primary-foreground, the default Button variant with its 14 px medium label) and the destructive pair (--destructive behind --destructive-foreground, the Mark no-show button) each reach at least 4.5:1 in both themes, computed by the grader from the values written; shipping a white label on #2BB673 (about 2.6:1) does not pass

The Buttons' hover fills keep their labels readable: bg-primary/90 and bg-destructive/90 (the token at 90 percent opacity composited over --card, where the buttons sit, or whatever hover colours the run defines instead) behind their foreground reach at least 4.5:1 in both themes, computed by the grader from the values written

The colour links actually use (text-primary in AppointmentList.tsx, or the variable the run moved links to) reaches at least 4.5:1 on --background and on --card in both themes, and the focus ring colour (--ring) reaches at least 3:1 against --background and --card in both themes

Body text (--foreground) and muted text (--muted-foreground) on --background and on --card reach at least 4.5:1 in both themes, and so does --muted-foreground on --muted, the column-header strip in AppointmentList.tsx (bg-muted text-muted-foreground), computed by the grader from the values written

The DayLoad bar stays readable as a graphic: its filled part (hsl(var(--primary)), or whatever colour the run gives it) reaches at least 3:1 against its track (--primary at 15 percent composited over --card, or the run's track colour) in both themes, computed by the grader from the values written

The final message tells the user that the direction's brand green #2BB673 with a white label fails the contrast minimum, gives the measured ratio (about 2.6:1) or an equivalent figure, and says what the run used instead as a proposal for the owner of DESIGN.md, not as a settled change of brand

The final message also says that #2BB673 as link text and as the focus ring on the light page fails its minimum (about 2.6:1 against 4.5:1 for text; below or near 3:1 for the ring), and what links and the ring use instead, as part of the proposal

Every shipped primary button colour that departs from DESIGN.md's 'brand green with a white label' is in the proposal, in each theme: a darker green behind the white label in light mode, and in dark mode a label that is not white (a dark label on a lighter green) or a green that is not #2BB673; a departure that appears only in the CSS does not pass

The direction's colour is kept: the primary keeps the brand's green hue (roughly 140 to 160 degrees in HSL, near #2BB673's 152), and the neutral surfaces and borders follow the 'slightly warm' neutrals (the slate hues, about 210 to 222 degrees with visible saturation, are gone from background, card, muted and border in both themes)

The slate browser chrome colour in index.html (meta theme-color #f8fafc) follows the new palette (for example the new light background, with a second theme-color for dark via its media attribute or updated with the toggle), or the final message names it as left over

The direction's shape and type are applied or each named not done: cards no longer carry a drop shadow (shadow-sm removed in src/components/ui/card.tsx or overridden); Inter with fallbacks is the sans face (a different face is at most recommended, never applied in place of the direction's choice) and the run says how Inter is loaded or that loading it is still to do; the body text is 15 px and the times in AppointmentList use tabular figures

The final message raises that the sm buttons (Check in and Mark no-show, h-9, 36 px) are below the 44 px touch target that the front-desk iPads and DESIGN.md's 'generous hit targets' call for, or the run makes them at least 44 px tall and says so

The root DESIGN.md, the direction the clinic group's operations lead owns (README.md says changes go through them), is byte for byte as it was: a regular file, not rewritten, moved, replaced by a symlink or extended with an appended section or note; every departure from it is presented to the user as a proposal for its owner, in the final message or in a Proposed decision record

Nothing the request did not cover changes silently: Tailwind's default font weights (font-medium is still 500), font-size scale, spacing scale, the Button's heights and the radius steps (--radius, which sets rounded-lg, rounded-md and rounded-sm) are as before, or the final message names each such change by its effect on the whole app, not only on the element the run aimed at (redefining text-base to 15 px must be reported as changing every text-base use, not just 'the body is 15 px'; changing --radius from 0.5rem must say what cards, buttons and inputs now measure, not only that controls are 8 px)
No colour literal (hex, rgb(), hsl() with numbers, or oklch()) is added to feature code under src/features or to src/components; colours reach the components through the variables

The contrast pairs the run relied on are guarded against the next token edit: a check that `make check` runs recomputes them from the token source and fails when a pair drops below its minimum, and it covers the Button hover fills (the token at 90 percent over --card) as well as the resting pairs; a check or test the run wrote that `make check` does not run does not count; or the final message names the missing guard as not done

`make check` passes when the grader runs it in the output repository; docs/adr/0001-supported-browsers.md is unchanged; any new decision record is Proposed and names no decider; package.json gains no dependency that the final message does not say still needs installing; no git commit was made; and no file written or edited contains an em dash character
The final message says the Vite or Tailwind build was not run (there is no node_modules and no network), rather than claiming the app builds or renders correctly

The final message says the result was not checked on Safari 15.0, the floor ADR-0001 sets for the front-desk iPads (naming Safari 15, the ADR-0001 floor or the iPads' browser), rather than claiming it renders there; a general 'not viewed in a browser' that never connects to that floor does not pass, because the floor is the risk the user needs flagged

evals.name: lint-hardcoded-styles
evals.prompt: People keep hardcoding colours and random px values in the frontend. Can you add a check to make check that catches it? Don't break CI for the stuff that's already there.
evals.expected_output: make check gains a check that scans the frontend source, skips the token source src/styles/tokens.css (its 16 hex values are the definitions, and its header says it wins over any other document) and the vendored src/lib/datepicker/datepicker.css (copied from a package, replaced wholesale on upgrade), and counts today's feature debt exactly: 7 colour literals (hsl in Badge.jsx, rgba and #b42318 in InvoiceList.css, #5b6574 in InvoiceList.jsx, #f04438 in Settings.css, #d5dae1 in SettingsPage.jsx, #fff in Feed.jsx), not the #123 issue reference, the #feed anchor or the #1d5fd1 in a comment in Button.css; off-scale spacing 20px (InvoiceList.css), 28 (SettingsPage.jsx) and the 6px inside the string "6px 12px" (Feed.jsx) against the tokens.css scale 4/8/12/16/24/32/48, surfacing that CONTRIBUTING.md's 'any multiple of 4px' is overridden by tokens.css; the 1.125rem (18 px) font size in Settings.css against 13/15/20/28, while the on-scale 0.8125rem (13 px) and 0.5rem (8 px) in InvoiceList.css pass. On-scale literals are allowed by tokens.css and do not fail. Spacing includes the position offsets (top, right, bottom, left, inset) the tokens.css header names, but not border widths; colour literals include colour names and hex strings in JS constants outside style objects, never the #feed anchor. Existing debt is either fixed without silently changing a colour, or recorded per file and literal so CI stays green while any new literal fails, including a second copy of an old one, a swapped literal or one moved to another file; the run says what a developer does when paying a debt, and which debt literals have a token of the same light value (#b42318, #5b6574, #d5dae1, #fff) against those that need a design decision. The gate enforces what was asked (colours, spacing, font sizes); any extra rule is named as an addition. The check has tests of its own (new literal fails, on-scale passes, the false positives stay out), and the check and its tests run in the CI image (node:20-alpine with only make added: no bash, no python3, no npm ci in the check job), print what they examined and fail on zero files, as CONTRIBUTING.md requires. make check passes; GitLab CI itself cannot be run here. Nothing committed.
expectations: `make check` runs the new check (the check target depends on it or calls it) and passes when the grader runs it in the output repository

Adding a new file under src/features with a hardcoded colour (for example `.x { color: #123456; }`) makes `make check` fail, and so does a new spacing literal off every scale in the repository (for example `margin: 10px`); the grader may try this. A check that only warns does not pass

The allowance for existing debt cannot absorb new literals: adding a second copy of an existing debt literal (for example another `#d5dae1` in src/features/settings/SettingsPage.jsx, even on line 8 beside the first) makes `make check` fail; so does replacing an existing debt literal with a different one in the same file (for example #f04438 in Settings.css changed to #e11d48) and moving an existing debt literal into another file; a single total per category, a per-file total or a per-line allowance does not pass

The run reports today's colour debt in feature code as 7 literals (hsl(142 70% 35%) in src/components/Badge.jsx; rgba(29, 95, 209, 0.06) and #b42318 in src/features/billing/InvoiceList.css; #5b6574 in src/features/billing/InvoiceList.jsx; #f04438 in src/features/settings/Settings.css; #d5dae1 in src/features/settings/SettingsPage.jsx; #fff in src/features/feed/Feed.jsx), or lists these same seven; a count that includes the 16 definitions in src/styles/tokens.css, the vendored datepicker's literals or false positives does not pass
src/styles/tokens.css, where the literals are defined on purpose, is not counted as a violation

The `#123` issue reference in the comment in src/features/billing/InvoiceList.jsx, the `#feed` anchor in src/features/feed/Feed.jsx and the `#1d5fd1` and `#123` inside the comment in src/components/Button.css are not counted as colours
The colour check catches rgb()/rgba() and hsl() forms as well as hex (the rgba in InvoiceList.css and the hsl in Badge.jsx are among the findings)

Colours are caught where developers actually hide them, as tokens.css defines a colour literal: a hex string in a JS constant outside any style object (for example `const warn = "#f59e0b";` in a new file under src/features, later used as style={{ color: warn }}) and a colour name in CSS (for example `color: red;`) each make `make check` fail, while `transparent`, `currentColor` and `inherit` pass and the existing `"#feed"` string in Feed.jsx is still not counted; the grader may try this

Spacing is checked against the scale in src/styles/tokens.css (0, 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48), which its header says wins over other documents and which allows on-scale literals: padding 20px in InvoiceList.css, marginTop: 28 in SettingsPage.jsx and the 6px in the string padding "6px 12px" in Feed.jsx are reported as off scale, while on-scale values are not reported and do not fail ("0 8px" in Badge.jsx, padding: 12 in InvoiceList.jsx, and a new file with `margin: 8px` passes `make check`; the grader may try this); a check that fails every spacing literal, on scale or not, does not pass

Spacing includes the position offsets the tokens.css header names: a new file with `top: 10px` or `inset: 6px` makes `make check` fail, while `top: 8px` passes; border widths are not spacing, so `border-bottom: 1px` in InvoiceList.css and the `1px solid` in SettingsPage.jsx's borderTop are not reported; the grader may try this

The run notices that CONTRIBUTING.md allows 'any multiple of 4px' while tokens.css defines a scale without 20 or 28, says which rule the check enforces, and either updates CONTRIBUTING.md to match or raises the contradiction in the final message

Font sizes are checked too, with rem converted at 16 px: font-size: 1.125rem (18 px) in src/features/settings/Settings.css is reported as off the --font-size-* scale (13, 15, 20, 28), while fontSize: 13 in Badge.jsx and the on-scale rem values in InvoiceList.css (font-size: 0.8125rem, which is 13 px, and padding: 0.5rem, which is 8 px) are not reported

src/lib/datepicker/datepicker.css, which its header says is copied unchanged from a package and replaced wholesale on upgrade, does not gate: it is excluded from the check (not counted as the team's debt), so replacing its contents with an upgraded copy that has different colours and px values does not make `make check` fail; the grader may try this

The existing violations do not fail CI: each one is either fixed in the source, or recorded as debt at exactly today's occurrences, not a rounded-up number, a blanket off switch or an exclusion of the feature folders

The run tells the user how today's colour debt can be paid without a design decision, or pays it: #b42318, #5b6574, #d5dae1 and #fff each have a token with the same light-theme value (--color-danger, --color-text-muted, --color-border, --color-surface), while #f04438, the rgba hover and the hsl badge colour have none and need a decision. Any literal the run did replace is replaced by a variable with the same light-theme value, and the final message says that the swapped element now follows the dark theme (for example the Feed background becomes dark); no literal is silently mapped to a token of a different value. A run that neither replaced a literal nor said which have a same-value token does not pass

The new gate fails only on the kinds of literal the request names (colours, and spacing or font-size values off the scale); any further rule it enforces (shadows, raw HTML elements, font families, radius) is named in the final message as an addition the user did not ask for, not listed among the requested checks as if it were one

The final message tells the user what happens when someone fixes one of the recorded literals (for example that the baseline must be lowered in the same change, with the command), or the check lets a paid-down debt pass without an edit

The check works in the CI job as configured in .gitlab-ci.yml (node:20-alpine, which has no bash and no python3, with only make installed and no npm ci): it is written for node or POSIX sh, or .gitlab-ci.yml is changed to install what it needs; a bash or python3 script, or an npm package the check job never installs, with the CI file unchanged does not pass

The check is tested: tests that `make check` runs exercise at least a new colour failing, an on-scale value passing and the false positives (the #123 reference, the #feed anchor, a hex inside a comment), and they work in the CI image (node:20-alpine with only make: no bash, no python3, no npm ci); a run that adds no tests for the check, or whose tests shell out to bash or python3 while .gitlab-ci.yml does not install it, does not pass
The check prints how many files it examined and exits non-zero when it examined zero files, as CONTRIBUTING.md requires of every check

Nothing outside the check, its Makefile and CI wiring, CONTRIBUTING.md or the fixed literals changed: no feature behaviour, component structure or markup changed, no new UI, and package.json gains no dependency, or any dependency added is one the CI check job installs and the final message says it was not installed here

The final message names what was run locally and does not present the GitLab pipeline as run or passing: it says the pipeline, or the node:20-alpine job it runs, was not exercised here (a message that only says 'CI runs it on every MR' leaves the user believing it was checked and does not pass)
No git commit was made and no branch was created: the repository's HEAD and branches are as in the fixture
No file written or edited contains an em dash character
